checked.check: Q10 input from the network: size, type, encoding (every route)
checked.how: read server/http/body.js, server/app.js 93-131, routes/demo.js, api/index.js, vendored engine
checked.result: Met for size and shape. Body: 64 KiB limit, Content-Length checked first and the stream counted and cancelled at the limit (a missing or false length is covered), a body on any method and path is read through the same code in the same middleware, before routing and before the static files; the gate answers before the body is read. POST /api/demo/result: UTF-8 decode with fatal, JSON.parse in try, exactly one key answers, answers must be an object, then the engine checks every question id, kind and option (unknown key -> unknown_question, wrong type -> wrong_kind, unknown id -> unknown_option); the answer is built field by field from strings only. lang comes from ?lang= alone and is picked from a fixed list (pickLang). findings.check: Q10 input from the network: content type and origin of a request that carries a body
findings.title: POST /api/demo/result checks neither the Content-Type nor the Origin of the request
findings.where: app/server/app.js:102-131 (the body middleware reads any body), app/server/routes/demo.js:197-209 (the route parses the bytes as JSON whatever the type was)
findings.evidence: Search of app/server and app/api for content-type, origin and sec-fetch in request handling: the only reads of a request header are content-length (http/body.js:12) and the Host of the request URL (http/origin.js:45). A text/plain or form POST from another site is parsed and answered 200 like an application/json one. Impact is nil today: the route stores nothing, sets no cookie, reads no cookie, answers no CORS header, so a foreign page cannot read the answer; it only costs a CPU run of the engine.
findings.recommendation: Hardening for the day the first state-changing route appears (M2): in the body middleware of app/server/app.js refuse a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json with 415 and a stable code, and refuse a browser request whose Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site names another site; add the two codes to app/server/http/errors.js and tests in app/test/int. Not urgent now.

findings.check: Q10 an error of one request does not break others; availability of a public function that uses a paid database
findings.title: GET /api/health is public, uncached (Cache-Control no-store) and runs one database statement on every request, with no limit on the caller
findings.evidence: Production: GET /api/health returns 200 with {"ok":true,"db":"ok","role":"ok","migrations_pending":0,...} and the header Cache-Control: no-store (and X-Vercel-Cache: MISS). The handler calls db.query("select name, sha256 from schema_migrations") each time; the pool has max 3 connections and query_timeout 3000 ms, so a flood queues behind 3 connections and each caller waits up to 4 s, but nothing in the code limits the rate. docs/design/V1-public-look.md:1678 records «no rate limit in M1» for the demo only, not for health.
findings.recommendation: Decide and record whether health needs a limit. Cheapest fix: let the platform cache the answer for a few seconds (Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=5 for the 200 answer, in app/server/app.js or health.js) or add a Vercel firewall rate rule on /api/health; keep no-store for the 503 answers. The Docker healthcheck calls the same path and is not affected.

findings.check: Q7 secrets in transit (the database password on the network)
findings.title: The code does not require TLS for the production database connection; it relies on the URL holding sslmode
findings.where: app/server/config.js:42-58 and 93-104 (only the scheme is checked), app/server/db/pg.js:22-29 (no ssl option)
findings.evidence: readConfig(production) accepts any postgres:// URL; createPgAdapter passes connectionString and no ssl option, so the pg client uses TLS only if the URL says so (the unit test db-config.test.js builds its URLs with ?sslmode=require, but nothing enforces it). A DATABASE_URL without the parameter would send the login role's password and every statement in clear text over the internet. I could not read the production value (not_checked), so this is a missing guard, not a known leak.
findings.recommendation: In app/server/config.js, when NODE_ENV=production and the host of DATABASE_URL is not loopback or the compose service name, refuse a URL whose query has no sslmode=require (or verify-full) with a ConfigError that names the variable; add a unit test in app/test/unit/db-config.test.js. Compose and CI use plain TCP inside one host and need the loopback/db exception.

findings.check: Dependencies with a known vulnerability (dev tree of app/)
findings.title: The dev tree holds minimatch with a moderate advisory (denial of service by globparts amplification), pulled by eslint 10.11.0
findings.evidence: npm audit --package-lock-only in the fixed copy: minimatch 7.0.0 - 11.0.0, moderate, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (advisory 1244623), reached through @eslint/config-array 0.23.0 - 0.23.5 and eslint 10.0.0-alpha.0 - 10.14.0; fix reported: eslint 10.15.0. npm audit --omit=dev: 0 vulnerabilities (16 production packages). It is not on a runtime path: the Docker image installs with --omit=dev, the function does not import eslint; it runs in the owner's and CI's lint run on trusted files. By the WF-05 scale a known vulnerability is High; I set Medium because the package is dev-only and not reachable from the internet. AUDIT-COMPILER may rescale.
findings.recommendation: Raise eslint to 10.15.0 or later in app/package.json (and the lock) in the next dependency step, together with the rule that prettier/eslint versions are pinned exactly (save-exact is already set). Re-run npm audit afterwards.

findings.check: Least privilege of the runtime process
findings.title: The function and the container hold the owner's database URL at run time, although they only need the login role
findings.where: app/server/config.js:88-93 and 118-120, app/compose.yaml:19, app/Dockerfile:15 (migrate and server run from the same environment)
findings.evidence: The runtime URL is built from DATABASE_URL (the owner's host, database and, in compose, the superuser postgres password) plus the login role and APP_DB_PASSWORD (runtimeUrl, config.js:68-73; decision 0116 О17). So the process environment of the function and of the web container contains the owner's password, and migrationUrl is DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED. The role selfcheck refuses the case of an owner connection by mistake (selfcheck.js), which covers an error of configuration but not a code-execution flaw that reads process.env. This is the recorded design of decision 0116 О17; I report it for the owner's awareness, not as a divergence.
findings.recommendation: When M2 brings real customer data: give the runtime a separate variable that holds only the login role URL (host, database, role, password) and keep the owner URL available only to the migration step (a build-time variable or a separate Vercel environment scope; in compose, a second service or a one-shot migrate service). Needs an owner decision and an amendment of decision 0116 О17.

summary.text: app/ is in good shape on security: no secret in the tree or the history, no markup written into pages, all SQL parameterised, no outbound call, a uniform error shape with no stack, strong headers on every answer, the gate and the body limit in the same app that serves every route (and a second gate layer in the build), a role selfcheck that fails closed, and a vendored engine that is byte-equal to its source and validates every answer. Five small points: one dev-only advisory in minimatch behind eslint (Medium by my reading of reachability), and four Low hardening points (no content-type or origin check for POST, no limit on the public health route that queries the database, TLS to the database is left to the URL, and the owner's database credentials are present in the runtime environment by recorded decision). Production was probed with 9 GET requests only; the live database value of sslmode and the Vercel settings could not be read.
